notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: read herbdata.Rd (a 1994 herbicide trial in southwestern Washington, three replications of 20 seedlings in a control block and a block treated with Oust, each seedling's basal diameter, height and status recorded at eight visits over ten years; Robinson and Hamann 2010) and the book code the package ships, inst/resources/scripts/book/data_management.r: it only plots height against basal diameter by treat and rep and by treat and date, divides CONTROL rep B's dia and dbh at the seventh visit by 2.54 as misrecorded units, and sums basal areas per plot; no model. Growth is rendered by treatment over date as a categorical visit. A seedling is treat:tree, since tree runs 1-60 within each treatment block (rep A 1-20, B 21-40, C 41-60); rep is a usable design column, and the six treat:rep plots, which a blind second reading added as a grouping factor, are left out as a weak component. isalive is an alternate response, dia and dbh alternate size measures (dbh 0 below breast height); a dead stem's measures are NA. Treatment was applied to one block each, so treat and block coincide. Outside check: stands against the reply's plot intercept, by the weak-component ruling (#180).

formula: immun ~ kid2p + mom25p + ord + ethn + momEd + husEd + momWork + rural + pcInd81 + (1|mom) + (1|comm)
notes: Rodriguez and Goldman (2001, JRSS A 164, Table 2) fit three-level random-intercept logistic models of complete immunization, children within mothers within communities; Rodriguez's data page (grodri.github.io/research/guat) lists the file's predictors in Table 2's order, which mlmRev collapses into factors. kid is the child id. Stands alone: guPrenat is a different outcome table, not a companion. Outside check: the 2001 paper and its data page replace the recalled 1995 citation.

formula: prenat ~ childAge + motherAge + birthOrd + indig + momEd + husEd + husEmpl + toilet + TV + pcInd81 + ssDist + (1|mom) + (1|cluster)
notes: Rodriguez and Goldman (2001, JRSS A 164, Table 3) fit three-level random-intercept logistic models of modern prenatal care, births within mothers within communities; Rodriguez's data page (grodri.github.io/research/guat) lists the file's predictors in Table 3's order, which mlmRev collapses into factors. kid is the birth id. Outside check: the 2001 paper and its data page replace the recalled 1995 citation.

Read the help page (Hicks 1993): 9 teams, each of one physique, each tried both methods twice. Wood (2017, ch. 2 solution Q9; gamair 1.0-2 ch2.solutions.Rd) fits lme(rounds ~ Method + Physique, random = ~1 | Team), tests Physique and keeps m2 = lme(rounds ~ Method, random = ~1 | Team). Physique is a three-level design factor of the teams, not a grouping factor; Maindonald and Braun's exercise solution fits rounds ~ Physique/Method with the same Team intercept. Team codes (T1S to T3H) are unique. Outside check: Wood's final model replaces the Physique/Team nesting.

Read the help page (Diggle, Liang and Zeger 1994: protein content after calving under three diets); it gives no model. A statistical consulting tutorial (scsru.github.io/Modules/introduction-to-longitudinal-data.html, Example - Milk Protein and Diet) adds quadratic and cubic time terms by likelihood-ratio tests, finds no diet-by-time terms, drops the random time slope and keeps fitcows5 = lme(protein ~ D1 + D2 + Time + Timesq + Timecb, random = ~1 | Cow), D1 and D2 the diet dummies. Breheny and Burchett (2017, R Journal, visreg) illustrate lmer(protein ~ Diet + Time + (Time | Cow)). Outside check: the tutorial's selected model replaces the inferred one.

formula: deltaBP ~ four-parameter logistic in log(dose), A + (B - A)/(1 + exp((log(dose) - ld50)/th)), ld50 by Treatment; random A and ld50 by Rabbit and by Run within Rabbit
notes: NONLINEAR: Venables and Ripley (2002, sec. 10.3; MASS 7.3-66 scripts/ch10.R) fit MASS's copy of these data (Rabbit: BPchange, Dose, Animal, Run) with the four-parameter logistic Fpl(Dose, A, B, ld50, th): first per treatment (Rc.nlme, Rm.nlme, random A + ld50 ~ 1 | Animal), then R.nlme1 with every parameter by Treatment and random A + ld50 ~ 1 | Animal/Run, and last R.nlme2 with only ld50 by Treatment. Read PBG.Rd (App. A.21): five rabbits, each under Placebo and MDL 72222, increasing doses. Run (P1-P5, T1-T5) is the rabbit-by-treatment combination, its codes unique. Outside check: the final nonlinear model replaces the linear trend in log(dose).

Help page fits clm(rating ~ temp*contact) with no random effect. The clmm help (ordinal 2026.7-26) fits clmm(rating ~ temp + contact + (1|judge)), and the clmm2 tutorial fits the same model (fm1, fm2), then tests contact (fm3) and the judge effect (fm4). rating is the ordered 5-level grouping of the continuous column response (ignored). bottle (8 levels) is an unused usable column. Domain industry for the wine-production process factors (reporting only; could read as agriculture). Outside check: the documented additive model replaces the recalled interaction.

formula: I(1000/rt) ~ F*P*Q*lQ*lT + (1 + Q | subj) + (0 + I(as.numeric(lT) - 1.5) | subj) + (1 | item) + (0 + I(as.numeric(P) - 1.5) | item)
notes: Masson, Rabe & Kliegl 2017 (Exp. 1) masked-priming lexical decision, subj x item crossed; factors F (frequency), P (semantic priming), Q (stimulus quality), lQ/lT (previous-trial quality/type), response rt in ms. trial is the trial-sequence index, ignored. SMLP2024's mrk17 page (repsychling.github.io/SMLP2024/mrk17.html, sec. 6.1) replicates the paper's linear mixed model as m_mrk17_crossed: (1000 / rt) ~ 1 + F*P*Q*lQ*lT + (1 + Q | subj) + zerocorr(0 + lT | subj) + zerocorr(1 + P | item), every factor in effects coding; the formula writes the zerocorr slopes as centered numeric codes. random_slopes writes lT|subj as correlated, since a factor's slopes are all | or all ||. Outside check: the published model replaces the main-effects reading.

pingouin cochran() docstring runs Cochran's Q test (dv=Energetic, within=Time, subject=Subject); energy level across three days (real-statistics.com). Cochran's Q is a nonparametric test and fits no model, so the random-intercept logistic model is a proposal from the design. Outside check: published_model turns no.

The page says only that the data are cross-classified. mlmRev 1.0-9's tests/lmerTest.R fits fmS1 = lmer(attain ~ verbal * sex + (1|primary) + (1|second)) and compares it with fmS3 (no interaction) and fmS4 (a sex slope by second). Outside check: the package's test replaces the recalled lme4 example.

Read the help page (split-block design, Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.2). Pinheiro and Bates's ch04.R (nlme 3.1-171) fits fm1Assay = lme(logDens ~ sample * dilut, random = pdBlocked(list(pdIdent(~ 1), pdIdent(~ sample - 1), pdIdent(~ dilut - 1)))), independent block, block:sample and block:dilut intercepts in lme4 syntax. Only 2 blocks. Pilot re-filing: grouping factor Block:dilut built by the merge from its parts. Outside check: stands.

Read the help page (Hand and Crowder; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.3), which gives only the groupedData structure weight ~ Time | Rat. Pinheiro and Bates's ch05.R (nlme 3.1-171) fits fm1BW.lme = lme(weight ~ Time * Diet, random = ~ Time); fm2BW.lme and fm3BW.lme add a varPower variance and an exponential correlation, the fixed and random parts unchanged. Diet is constant within rat. Outside check: stands.

Read the help page (one row per student, no model). Maindonald and Braun's solution to chapter 9 exercise 7 (Data Analysis and Graphics Using R, 1st ed.) fits lme(MathAch ~ Minority * Sex * (MEANSES + SES), random = ~1 | School) on MathAchieve. Raudenbush and Bryk's model takes Sector from MathAchSchool, which this table lacks, and Pinheiro and Bates's scripts fit no MathAchieve model. MEANSES is school-level (constant within School). Outside check: the exercise solution replaces the recalled model.

Read the help page (Cochran and Cox 1957: roasts in pairs, pairs in blocks, balanced incomplete block design); Pair codes embed the block (II-1), so Pair is a column whose codes do not repeat across blocks. Treatment Storage is fixed. No published fitted model located. Outside check: stands; the help names tenderness as the experiment's response, so the response is not inferred.

Read the help page (Yates 1935 split-plot; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.15; Venables and Ripley 2002): 6 blocks, whole plots of Variety, subplots of nitro. Pinheiro and Bates's ch01.R (nlme 3.1-171) fits fm1Oats = lme(yield ~ ordered(nitro) * Variety, random = ~1 | Block/Variety), drops the interaction (fm2Oats) and Variety (fm3Oats), and ends with fm4Oats = lme(yield ~ nitro, random = ~1 | Block/Variety), nitro linear; ch04.R refits fm4Oats with other block covariances. Block:Variety (the whole plot) has no column. Pilot re-filing: grouping factor Block:Variety built by the merge from its parts. Outside check: the final model replaces the first fit.

Read the help page (its example is only formula(Orthodont), i.e. distance ~ age | Subject; Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App A.17). Pinheiro and Bates's ch04.R (nlme 3.1-171) fits fm2Orth.lme = lme(distance ~ Sex * I(age - 11), random = ~ I(age - 11) | Subject), the same model with age centered, and fm3Orth.lme adds a residual variance by Sex; comparePred's example fits distance ~ age * Sex with random = ~ age. Sex is constant within Subject. Outside check: stands.

Read Oxboys.Rd (App. A.19); Pinheiro and Bates's ch03.R only builds the groupedData. Tierney's talk (R: An Overview and Some Current Directions, Korean Statistical Society 2006, slide 18) fits lme(height ~ age, data = Oxboys, random = ~ age | Subject). Occasion is an ordered recoding of age, ignored. Outside check: the talk replaces the recalled book fit.

Read Oxide.Rd (App. A.20, Littell et al. 1996 p. 155): variance-components study, wafers nested in lots. Pinheiro and Bates's ch04.R (nlme 3.1-171) fits fm1Oxide = lme(Thickness ~ 1, Oxide) through its Lot/Wafer grouping and compares it with fm2Oxide (Lot only); Wood (2017, ch. 2 Q6) adds Site and Source. Wafer codes repeat across lots; Source and Site left as unused columns. Regrouped by #45: the nested factor named as its composite, its codes repeating across its parent. Outside check: stands.
Read Rail.Rd (App. A.26; Devore 2000 Ex. 10.10). Pinheiro and Bates's ch01.R (nlme 3.1-171) fits fm1Rail.lme = lme(travel ~ 1, random = ~ 1 | Rail). Outside check: stands.

Read RatPupWeight.Rd (no model, no examples). West, Welch and Galecki's chapter 3 code (WWGbook 1.0.2, inst/scripts/ch03.R) starts from weight ~ treatment * sex + litsize with a litter intercept (Model 3.1), lets the residual variance differ between control and treated litters (Model 3.2B), drops treatment:sex and ends with Model 3.3, the final model: lme(weight ~ sex + litsize + treatment, random = ~1 | litter, weights = varIdent(form = ~1 | trtgrp)). Hernandez's tutorial fits Models 3.1 and 3.2A. Treatment, Lsize constant within litter. Outside check: the book's final model replaces the recalled one with the interaction.

formula: logSize ~ days + (1 | plot) + (1 | Tree) + a penalized smoothing spline in days, its coefficients iid random
notes: Read Spruce.Rd (App. A.28; Diggle et al. 1994 Ex. 1.3); the page gives no model, and the ozone treatment is not a column. Tree codes (O1T01) encode the plot, so Tree is nested in plot. smspline's examples (lmeSplines 1.1-12) fit spruce.fit1 = lme(logSize ~ days, random = list(all = pdIdent(~ Zday - 1), plot = ~1, Tree = ~1)), Zday the spline basis in days with one common variance over a constant level, compare it with spruce.fit2 (a plot-level slope and spline) and summarize spruce.fit1. The spline stays in the formula only. plot has four levels. Outside check: the spline model replaces its linear simplification.

formula: current ~ voltage + I(voltage^2) + cos(4.5679*voltage) + sin(4.5679*voltage) + (1 + voltage + I(voltage^2) || Wafer) + (1 + voltage + I(voltage^2) || Wafer:Site)
notes: Read Wafer.Rd (no model, no details). Pinheiro and Bates's ch04.R (nlme 3.1-171) fits fm1Wafer = lme(current ~ voltage + I(voltage^2), random = list(Wafer = pdDiag(~ voltage + I(voltage^2)), Site = pdDiag(~ voltage + I(voltage^2)))), then fm2Wafer, which adds cos(4.5679*voltage) + sin(4.5679*voltage) with the same uncorrelated random effects; fm3Wafer and fm4Wafer, general covariances, are commented out of the script, and ch08.R fits a nonlinear cosine model (fm2Wafer.nlme). Site codes 1-8 repeat across wafers. Quadratic and periodic terms filed as covariate voltage. Regrouped by #45: the nested factor named as its composite, its codes repeating across its parent. Outside check: fm2Wafer and its pdDiag slopes replace the recalled correlated fit.

Read bdf.Rd (Snijders and Bosker 1999). The mlbook scripts nlme 3.1-171 ships fit fm4 = lme(langPOST ~ IQ.ver.cen + avg.IQ.ver.cen, random = ~ 1 | schoolNR) in ch04.R (Table 4.4); ch05.R adds a random IQ slope (fm5, Table 5.1) and class size (fm6, Table 5.2). pupilNR is an id and aritPOST an alternate response. Column names contain dots, as loaded. Outside check: stands.
